{
  "reader": "a",
  "inputs_read": [
    "summary-snapshot.md",
    "questions.json"
  ],
  "answers": [
    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down and return the rest without looking; place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories; randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'one structure bonus tile'; 'lowest-numbered Player Mat starts'"},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"At setup, place the character on the home base; two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs over the faction abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the marked green Player Mat boxes; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement. The Faction Mat supplies starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat supplies starting popularity, coins, and two objectives.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup piece table and steps 3–4"},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action, the top only, or top then bottom. You may not take bottom first and may not take either action more than once that turn; Rusviet may repeat a section from the previous turn but still takes its top and bottom at most once each. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before action; take as much or as little of exposed green-box benefits as desired. Bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: different section; optional top/bottom; full cost then optional benefit; Rusviet limit"},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce when uncontrolled. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, including when acting elsewhere.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone controls; opponents do not gain abilities; pay from any controlled territories"},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"On a normal Move, the two selections must be different units, so one unit cannot move twice. A transported worker may subsequently move itself, or a worker may move onto a mech and be carried in its later move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, and may never carry your character.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: 'two different units'; carried worker may subsequently move; all units carry resources; mechs carry workers, never character"},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"The character or mech may enter enemy-worker-only territory but must stop and cannot move again that turn; the enemy workers immediately retreat home, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control it. Speed does not override this stop.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: Enemy workers only; 'Stops for enemy units ... override Speed'"},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"After all units finish movement, resolve all combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: Enemy character/mechs; 'Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action'; attacker chooses order"},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards to make a new deck, and if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Place traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster and Trade descriptions"},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production; then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades, and each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the cost just paid.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce steps 1–3; new workers from Player Mat left to right; may decline; future costs"},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; amounts vary by mat/upgrades. Upgrade moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy puts any mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all of these bottom-row goals, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Upgrade; Deploy; Bottom-row actions: may still pay after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits"},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents' structures, and Factory is allowed while lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. An enemy occupant does not gain your building's ability. Your Mine remains a personal tunnel for your unit movement even when enemy-controlled. A Mill provides its bonus production territory and may produce while controlled; it cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Build description; Control section: abilities retained except Mill cannot produce uncontrolled; Mine personal tunnel"},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat, immediately gaining two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, not the chosen one-time space. For the rest of the game it may trigger when you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom-row action. Resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs"},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Each combatant simultaneously and secretly selects dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and their current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army adds one card if workers are present). If both combatants have combat mech abilities, the attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously; add dial and card values, with attacker winning ties. Both players deduct selected dial power from the Power Track and discard played cards face-up; card values do not deduct extra track power.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–4"},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"The winner controls the territory and resources. All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units/carried workers to retreat to an adjacent lake instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat; a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie's stated combat exception. A non-Saxony winner places a combat star if they have zero or one such star, and none if they already have two; Saxony must place one after each victory while it has star tokens. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power via dial or cards; a zero-total loser draws none.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 5–6"},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard token and draw the card. If the character loses contested entry/combat, it retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs, and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action costs or mat benefits apply, including ongoing recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters paragraph: after whole Move and all combats; contested entry lost; gains to encounter territory; no additional normal action costs or mat benefits"},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. This is not limited to the first visitor; each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section, optional top then bottom subject to normal no-repeat rules (Rusviet exception), and gives no matching Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and ordinary movement/stop restrictions apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Factory section"},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action; you may wait but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is available; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements"},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Goals are awarded once except two combat stars and Saxony's exception; another player's stars never block a goal. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars and immediate end"},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star each time; if an earlier player placed the sixth, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sixth star sequence and pending battle rule"},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete pair of resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as 7, adding $21; 13 resources make 6 complete pairs, adding $12. These categories add $53 to held coins, plus any selected structure bonus. Structures are eligible for that bonus even if enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers are workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed. The structure-bonus amount cannot be determined without the selected tile and your structures.","support":"partial","evidence":"Final fortune: 7–12 tier table; Factory counts 3; resource pairs; structure eligibility; tie order"},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"A home base is not a territory for game effects. By default, you cannot move into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup, forced retreats, and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Expansion placeholder bases without a matching core faction are inactive.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases"},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce terrain table; resources section"},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"All units may pick up, carry, and drop off any number of resources during movement; only mechs may carry your workers, never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra step usable before or after it. Mechs can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: carrying; Speed; tunnel jump; stop rule"},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes. Any unit may enter a territory with only an enemy structure and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: Enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories"},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"You cannot pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, move your token to a different section and take neither action; after last using Move, choose another section for this dead turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: dead turn; never pay only part of a cost"},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are bonuses on those matching top actions. You keep structure abilities even without control of the territory; enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bolster; Trade; Control section; Build bonuses"},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"Riverwalk is a separate unlocked mech ability for every faction, including Nordic, and lets your character and all mechs cross rivers onto faction-specific destinations: Nordic and Saxony forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. It does not apply to workers. Nordic Swim is a starting ability for workers alone to cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not provide mech movement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Riverwalk table and faction ability table"},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including your Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Neither shortcut is stated for workers.","support":"supported","evidence":"Other unlocked mech abilities: Saxony Underpass; Rusviet Township"},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery applies before combat and lets you pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, once per combat, not per unit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery descriptions"},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"Two mechs and three workers allow three cards total with Rusviet People's Army: one additional card total if at least one worker is present, on top of one per participating character/mech. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rusviet People's Army; combat card rule; workers alone never fight"},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot move them to an active opponent's home base.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Wayfare description"},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of its value.","support":"supported","evidence":"Crimea Scout; Coercion descriptions"},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers with them. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; Polania has no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off, and carried workers or resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.","support":"supported","evidence":"Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge; lake carrying rules"},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not prevent loss for driving out undefended workers without combat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Polania Camaraderie description"},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Polania Meander allows choosing up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first gain may pay the second option's cost; pay each printed cost and you may take as little benefit as desired.","support":"supported","evidence":"Faction table: Meander; Encounters: option costs and benefit choice"},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"No. A character entering an encounter-token territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter after the whole Move action and all combats, not before combats finish, if the character remains there.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move encounter stop; Encounters timing; Factory rules apply during Factory Move"},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"Combat card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal whether you committed cards until reveal; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective. Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked.","support":"supported","evidence":"Public and hidden information table"},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"Players may make informal, unenforceable agreements; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable, and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat occurs after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.","support":"supported","evidence":"Objectives and agreements"},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"Popularity 0–6 pays $3 per star, $2 per territory count, and $1 per resource pair; 7–12 pays $4, $3, and $2 respectively; 13–18 pays $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a single leftover resource does not score.","support":"supported","evidence":"Final fortune popularity table; controlled locations; complete pairs"},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"For adjacency tiles, count each qualifying feature once across all your structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Tunnels means unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines. Encounters count unique printed encounter locations even if the token was removed. Lakes count unique lakes. Payout for tunnels, lakes, and encounters alike: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; tunnels reach 6 for $9, while lakes and encounters reach 6–7 for $9. Zero qualifying features score zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus eligibility table and adjacency rules"},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pays $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it; 1 pays $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts the combined qualifying structures; 1 pays $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.","support":"supported","evidence":"Structure bonus eligibility table"},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity for every enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat step 6"},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"No. A placed star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so placing a popularity star does not protect the current popularity level or its scoring tier if popularity later drops. Another player's star never blocks your goal, so two factions may both earn stars for the same achievement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars: permanent despite later drops; current popularity scores; other players' stars never block a goal"},
    {"id":"Q44","answer":"Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can trigger from your immediate left and right neighbors' matching bottom-row actions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 2; Ongoing recruits"},
    {"id":"Q45","answer":"A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. Ordinarily units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. A unit with applicable lake movement may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control/resources and home bases: river and lake definitions; Move movement rules"},
    {"id":"Q46","answer":"No, the encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud; you need not read every option aloud.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: show card; artwork; read capitalized text; options need not be read"},
    {"id":"Q47","answer":"There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control, resources and home bases: 'No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory'"},
    {"id":"Q48","answer":"The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player is deciding which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action"},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's exception only waives the previous-turn section restriction.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: chosen top and bottom actions limited once within turn, including Rusviet"},
    {"id":"Q50","answer":"You may choose the alternative to moving and gain $1.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1"},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. The summary specifically says that Produce workers are taken from the mat left-to-right and 'Workers never return to the Player Mat.' It does not state an additional separate worker-return procedure for retreat.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce: workers never return to the Player Mat; losing units retreat to home base"},
    {"id":"Q52","answer":"Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: 'You may attack with zero power/popularity'"},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no further combat star.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat star award: may still fight after reaching combat-star limit"},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: must choose one affordable option; unaffordable options cannot be selected; may take less benefit"},
    {"id":"Q55","answer":"Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. They reveal simultaneously after optionally adding cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat steps 1–3: simultaneously and secretly choose; reveal simultaneously"},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: 'Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses'"},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"No. Place a star as soon as you achieve its goal; a sixth star ends play immediately. A completed objective is specifically different: you may wait to reveal it, but must still meet every requirement at the moment you eventually reveal it, and normally only one objective star is available (Saxony can score both).","support":"supported","evidence":"Stars: place as soon as achieved; Objectives: may wait, requirements at reveal"},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Ordinarily, no character, mech, or worker can cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.","support":"supported","evidence":"Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; abilities provide exceptions"},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"No. The recruit is placed permanently on the chosen one-time recruit bonus and cannot later move.","support":"supported","evidence":"Enlist: 'It cannot later move'"},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"No. Only a character triggers an encounter. A character entering the token territory stops and later resolves the encounter if still there.","support":"supported","evidence":"Encounters: 'Only a character triggers an encounter'"},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"A controlled Mill adds one bonus production territory to your normal allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill counts as one producing worker and produces according to its terrain even with no actual worker there; each actual worker there may also produce normally, so its output is added, not substituted. It only provides production while controlled.","support":"supported","evidence":"Produce: Mill paragraph"},
    {"id":"Q62","answer":"You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, the summary provides no control basis for resources to preserve it. An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources.","support":"supported","evidence":"Control definition"},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.","support":"supported","evidence":"Bottom-row actions: 'Upgrade — oil ... Deploy — metal ... Build — wood ... Enlist — food'"}
  ]
}
EOF
",workdir:"/home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules",max_output_tokens:2000});
